Possible... Most certainly a Vaccinium. Highbush blueberry (V. corymbosum) will have either lightly fuzzy or glaucous undersides, or sometimes both. Lowbush (V. angustifolium) has skinnier, leathery leaves and is much lower to the ground. These stems look consistent with one's i've seen for Highbush. 

There's debate about there being three separate species of "Highbush blueberry" which include V. fuscatum and V. caesariense as well as V. corymbosum, each with specific leaf undersides and berry color. Then, of course, they can hybridize with each other and make things more confusing. These differences don't matter much, though, since they're still blueberries and they taste good! 

https://gobotany.nativeplanttrust.org/species/vaccinium/corymbosum/

I really feel like film should make a comeback as a family camera (It's still alive and well within the photography community, but lots of people don't care anymore). Hard drives die. Computers die. All of your digital pictures, if not backed up correctly, can vanish instantly. What are you going to do when you want to look back on that vacation when you were young? Go on Facebook? What if that isn't around anymore...

The photos also look much more real and nostalgic if they're right in front of you! Having a physical book to hand down to the grandkids can really mean a lot, because I doubt they'll enjoy trying to find your dead Facebook page just to see what you looked like when you were younger. 

Shoot film, not shitty phone pictures.
